From 1e2cc8c5e0745b545d4974788dc606d678b6e564 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Axel Lin <axel.lin@ingics.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jun 2019 21:26:31 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] regulator: lm363x: Fix off-by-one n_voltages for lm3632
 ldo_vpos/ldo_vneg

According to the datasheet https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm3632a.pdf
Table 20. VPOS Bias Register Field Descriptions VPOS[5:0]
Sets the Positive Display Bias (LDO) Voltage (50 mV per step)
000000: 4 V
000001: 4.05 V
000010: 4.1 V
....................
011101: 5.45 V
011110: 5.5 V (Default)
011111: 5.55 V
....................
100111: 5.95 V
101000: 6 V
Note: Codes 101001 to 111111 map to 6 V

The LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX should be 0b101000 (0x28), so the maximum voltage
can match the datasheet.

Fixes: 3a8d1a73a037 ("regulator: add LM363X driver")
Signed-off-by: Axel Lin <axel.lin@ingics.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190626132632.32629-1-axel.lin@ingics.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/regulator/lm363x-regulator.c b/drivers/regulator/lm363x-regulator.c
index 5647e2f97ff8..e4a27d63bf90 100644
--- a/drivers/regulator/lm363x-regulator.c
+++ b/drivers/regulator/lm363x-regulator.c
@@ -30,7 +30,7 @@
 
 /* LM3632 */
 #define LM3632_BOOST_VSEL_MAX		0x26
-#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x29
+#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x28
 #define LM3632_VBOOST_MIN		4500000
 #define LM3632_VLDO_MIN			4000000
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/regulator/lm363x-regulator.c`**
   - The constant `LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX` was modified from `0x29` to `0x28`. This change aligns the maximum voltage setting for the LM3632 LDO with the specifications outlined in the datasheet.

### Relationships

- The modification in `lm363x-regulator.c` directly addresses an off-by-one error in the voltage selection maximum for the LM3632 LDO, as indicated by the datasheet. This change is a bug fix that corrects the previously defined maximum voltage setting to ensure it accurately reflects the hardware capabilities, thereby improving the functionality of the LM363X driver. The patch is linked to a previous commit that introduced the LM363X driver, indicating that this fix is necessary for the correct operation of the driver.

Here is the commit message:
regulator: lm363x: Fix off-by-one n_voltages for lm3632
 ldo_vpos/ldo_vneg

According to the datasheet https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm3632a.pdf
Table 20. VPOS Bias Register Field Descriptions VPOS[5:0]
Sets the Positive Display Bias (LDO) Voltage (50 mV per step)
000000: 4 V
000001: 4.05 V
000010: 4.1 V
....................
011101: 5.45 V
011110: 5.5 V (Default)
011111: 5.55 V
....................
100111: 5.95 V
101000: 6 V
Note: Codes 101001 to 111111 map to 6 V

The LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX should be 0b101000 (0x28), so the maximum voltage
can match the datasheet.

Fixes: 3a8d1a73a037 ("regulator: add LM363X driver")
Signed-off-by: Axel Lin <axel.lin@ingics.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190626132632.32629-1-axel.lin@ingics.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect definition of the maximum voltage selection constant `LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX`, which was set to `0x29` instead of the correct value `0x28`. This discrepancy led to an off-by-one error in the voltage settings for the LM3632 LDO, resulting in potential misconfiguration of the voltage output based on the datasheet specifications.

Here is the patch:
 /* LM3632 */
 #define LM3632_BOOST_VSEL_MAX		0x26
-#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x29
+#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x28
 #define LM3632_VBOOST_MIN		4500000
 #define LM3632_VLDO_MIN			4000000

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x29
```
Reason:
The incorrect definition of `LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX` as `0x29` instead of the correct value `0x28` caused an off-by-one error in the voltage settings. This misconfiguration resulted in the potential for the LDO to output a voltage that exceeds the maximum specified in the datasheet, leading to incorrect operation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX		0x28
```
Reason:
Changing the definition of `LM3632_LDO_VSEL_MAX` to `0x28` aligns it with the datasheet specifications, ensuring that the maximum voltage selection corresponds correctly to the intended output voltage range for the LM3632 LDO, thus resolving the off-by-one error.
